assumptions: new videos all go to training; the 50/50 validation/test videos stay fixed
6 frames per video and the same pair-visual features as the 500-video run
Hugging Face download speed similar to the measured 9.2 MB/s AVA S3 rate (not measured for HF)
local frame extraction ~1 s/video for the whole-archive path (not measured)
graph build rate measured while Charades indexing shared the GPU; may be faster alone
training time scales linearly with training graphs at similar epoch counts
recommendation: Next step 2,000 videos (~1,500 more by range reads: ~1.5 h staging, ~0.6 h features, ~0.3 h training) and check the scaling curve; go to all 7,000 only if macro F1/mAP keep rising.
risks: RAM (estimate, not measured): the graph builder keeps every graph in memory and reloads the saved cache to verify it; the trainer torch.loads the whole cache. At 7,000 videos that is ~3.8 GB on disk and roughly 2x in peak RAM during build (~7-8 GB) on a 15.6 GB machine. Feasible but tight; 2,000 videos (~1.1 GB cache) carries no such risk.
Hugging Face throughput for whole archives is not measured; range reads measured 1.62 MB/s.
Validation/test stay at 50/50 videos, so per-predicate test support does not grow.
